events.intent: Grab the stone outcropping to stop my fall
events.response:
In a last ditch effort, you grab onto the stone ledge with both hands! But by 
now, you're moving much too fast, and the ledge disintegrates in a chalky cloud 
of stone dust.

"Good point there..." Rob the Guard clears his throat, searching for a good 
spot to continue from. "And when in the course of human events, eh, so and so 
and so and so...Ah, here we are!" He moves further down the scroll and resumes 
his proclamation. "...and since I, King Goosen, did not like his performance of 
'Ode to a Duck', feeling that it was inflammatory, I hereby banish him from my 
realm to spend the rest of his days in Orchestra Pit, unless he should die from 
the fall, as most people tend to do."

The ground approaches with maddening steadiness. Perhaps you should have been a 
carpenter... Or perhaps you just needed more than one song in your repertoire.

Up above, Jim leans over the edge of the pit, squinting. "Hallo down there! 
Where'd ye go?" He frowns and turns to Rob. "He must have already gotten eaten 
by the little devils... Poor fellow, he didn't even have a chance to shout out!"

"Indeed..." muses Rob.

The two continue their vigil into the pit for a few more minutes before 
deciding that nothing else will happen. "Ah well, Jim, there's always that lad 
involved in the pickle caper that we get to toss in next week! Come on, let's 
cover the pit back up!"

From your vantage point, you watch as the two guards struggle with a heavy 
metal hatch. There is a resounding clang as the hatch is locked into place and 
fourteen less-resounding clicks as the guards ensure that it will not be 
openable from the inside. A few more minutes pass and all sounds from above 
fade away. In the pale light which peeks around the hatch, you take stock of 
your new surroundings, resigned to your new dismal home.

running in from the north and around a sharp turn to the northeast. The light 
outlines a massive pile of uncut rocks against the south wall. In the midst of 
crumbled masonry, a large hole decorates the west wall, with stray rivulets of 
mud oozing from within like molten fudge.

by the little devils... Poor fellow, he didn't even have a chance to shout out!"

"Indeed..." muses Rob.

The two continue their vigil into the pit for a few more minutes before 
deciding that nothing else will happen. "Ah well, Jim, there's always that lad 
involved in the pickle caper that we get to toss in next week! Come on, let's 
cover the pit back up!"

metal hatch. There is a resounding clang as the hatch is locked into place and 
fourteen less-resounding clicks as the guards ensure that it will not be 
openable from the inside. A few more minutes pass and all sounds from above 
fade away. In the pale light which peeks around the hatch, you take stock of 
your new surroundings, resigned to your new dismal home.

Construction Office
This room consists of little more than a large stone counter before a doorway 
to the east. Behind the counter hangs an aged banner proclaiming, "Nolava Odd 
Community Construction Office". Beneath the banner someone has affixed a small 
day calendar. To the west, a dusty incline leads up into the quarry.

A tall bearded man in a black robe stalks into the room. Peering through the 
dust, he identifies you as the culprit. "Well I'll be! That wall from the pit 
must have finally broken down... we haven't had a visitor down here in years!" 
He rushes up to you, nearly bowling you over in the process, and shakes your 
hand furiously. "I am Leonine, the magician, and this is my home! Well 
actually, this is the Construction Office, but this little community is my home!
I moved down into this volcano when I became fed up with King Goosen up above. 
And if you got tossed in the pit...well, sniveling snails, you must be on my 
side of the bed! Are you odd?"

Leonine waits for a moment but continues on before you can answer. "This is the 
Nolava Odd Community and every permanent resident is a little odd, so if you're 
planning on sticking around, I'd suggest that you pick up some kind of 
idiosyncrasy, unless you just want to be mildly ill-tempered, which is just 
fine in my book as well. Of course, you won't have much company, since most of 
the residents are dead or moved away."

On the counter is a Building Codes manual.

from produce..." He tries again. "Clean Clothes!"

events.intent: Read the book
events.response:
You thumb through the book to find that only a few pages have entries on them...

To The Reader: It is my humble hope that this will one day be a definitive 
dictionary of music, preferably with a nice big number in front, perhaps 
"Finney's Book of Nine Billion, Eighty-Four Definitions of Music for the 
Layman", or maybe Infinite if I can write that much, but anyhow, I digress...

Cadence: The musical chords which outline a final resting point in a song. 
Personally I think cadences make music far too predictable so I usually only 
use one. And actually, in fifteen of my thirty-seven "Studies Only Using the 
Note F" I forwent a cadence entirely!

Embouchure: To people who play brass instruments, like the trumpet and tuba, 
the embouchure is the area of the lips that play into the mouthpiece. People 
with stronger embouchures have more playing endurance and can play difficult 
passages with ease.

Key: The tonal level of a piece of music. There are twelve major keys starting 
on each of twelve pitches between A and G. The major keys are the happy ones! 
There are also twelve minor keys, which start on the same pitches, for a grand 
total of 24 keys. Personally I like the keys of Ab minor and D major.

Overtones: These are the natural tones that are produced at various intervals 
over the pitch being playing. Though you can't always hear them enough to label 
them, they give every instrument a unique timbre.

Transposition: This is the act of taking a piece of music written in one key 
and rewriting it in a different key. One time, as an exercise, I transposed all 
four thousand of my G major sonatas to C# major. There isn't much to do down 
here.

Tritone: Also known as the augmented fourth or diminished fifth. The interval 
of notes that is the exact one half of an octave in the standard system. To the 
ear, its sound is easily recognizable, although one cannot tell whether the 
interval is an augmented fourth or a diminished fifth, since the two are the 
same sounding pitch. An example tritone is C to F# (augmented fourth) or C to 
Gb (diminished fifth), both of which sound the same. I once tried to write a 
piece exclusively in tritones. However, I ran out of new notes in the second 
measure, and initial reactions to the twelve minute piece were not very good.

Meanwhile, in King Goosen's Court...


Seated next to the dais, the Royal Scribe diligently takes notes as the King 
speaks.

"...let it be known that I am very pleased with the marked decline in 
popularity of ducks! I now decree that the ownership of ducks is illegal! 
Anyone who owns a duck, or is related to someone with a duck, or marries a 
duck, shall be publicly taunted and then cast out of society to live in my 
deepest dungeon, as soon as it is constructed. Thus I speak. Or spake." The 
exalted King wrings his hands. "I can never remember how to conjugate that 
dogged word! Royal Scribe!"

"Here, Your Highness...and still writing."

"Put in an addendum: The word speak shall always be conjugated as speak, 
henceforth and herewith!" The King rises from his throne and paces. "Let's 
see...I shall have to find a way to enforce my latest law... Royal Advisor!"

The scribe doffs his hat and puts another one on. "Advisor here, Your Highness!"

"How shall I enforce the duck ban? There shall be no ducks by sundown tomorrow."

The Advisor scratches his chin. "Perhaps you could place a duck in every home 
and then have the entire population arrested and deported. Saves the search 
time."

King Goosen ponders this intently for a moment and shakes his head. "There 
aren't enough ducks in the land to carry that out." He snaps. "I've got it! 
We'll use the same duck and recycle it. Advisor, take care of the details...I'm 
off to my morning Piddle Ball match!"

"Right-o." The Royal Advisor hurries off to enact the latest law while King 
Goosen of Papoosen prepares for Piddle Ball.

Meanwhile, in King Goosen's Court...


Morning sunlight peeks through the decorative flags in the upper gallery to 
show the King's Court in full attendance. Rows of commoners line each wall with 
guards enforcing order. Kneeling before the dais, one unlucky commoner speaks.

"But Your Majesty! The duck wasn't there the night before. I bet it was just my 
neighbour, Mr. Grindstaff." His voice drops to a furtive whisper. "If you must 
know, he's always been a duck sympathizer."

From the gallery, a voice rings out, evidently the aforementioned Mr. 
Grindstaff. "Choke on a turnip, ye yellow-bellied liar!"

"Silence, churlio!" A guard bangs his halberd on the marble floor. All eyes 
turn to the throne.

The King conveys a postcard image of wisdom before dispelling the illusion by 
speaking. "Your tale is obviously false, peasant. It's well-known that most 
duck owners keep their duck at the bottom of a moldy haystack where no one has 
tread for years, and that's exactly where we found yours. I sentence you to 
death and then deportation!"

The Advisor hurriedly whispers something in the King's ear. The royal personage 
looks crestfallen. "They can't, eh? Blast it all! You peasant! I sentence you 
to deportation, and maybe death, if you should happen to die along the way." 
The King snaps and the guards carry the pleading peasant away. He is quickly 
replaced by a more worldly man, also accused of harbouring a duck.

The King points at the man. "You sir, are accused of the same crime. What do 
you have to say for yourself?"

The man smiles craftily. "Obviously I own a duck. Your men found it buried 
under that boulder in my yard." The onlookers gasp as the man pleads guilty. He 
chuckles and leans in closer to the King. "What really has me worried, though, 
is this surge in the population of hamsters."

The King nods emphatically. "Actually, I find hamsters to be quite disagreeable 
little beasts. Always running this way and that...demanding food, shelter, and 
even immunity from property tax!"

"Indeed they are a nuisance," agrees the man. "In fact, I bet that owning a 
hamster is even worse than harbouring a duck!"

The King thinks about this new gem of knowledge and has a quick huddle with his 
Advisor. "Very well then. You, sir, are free to go on one condition! You must 
bring back more information about this hamster problem and the best way we can 
combat it! Dismissed!"

Meanwhile, in King Goosen's Court...


"...and in conclusion, unconfirmed sources have identified all hamsters as 
card-carrying un-Papoosenites." The worldly man ends his monologue with a bow 
and collapses into a seat brought up by the First Guard.

Unlikely for a man with an attention span shorter than the average armadillo 
snout, King Goosen has absorbed every word about the maledictions of the 
hamster cults. "We will obviously need to take charge against such an awesome 
threat! You sir, are now my officially appointed hamster Persecutor. You have 
full rights to organize campaigns of disinformation and terror until the 
hamster threat is quelled! By my royal word, all citizens who were on probation 
for harbouring ducks are now free, but on secondary limited probation. You may 
add these re-probates to your hamster patrol, and I grant you use of the brick 
building by the river as a headquarters for your operations. Now go, and do not 
return until our land is free of hamsters!"

"As you wish, Your Royal Highness." The worldly man grins shiftily and departs.

Back on the dais, the Royal Advisor tugs on the King's voluminous sleeve. "Your 
Highness...that building of which you spoke -"

"Speak," corrects the King. He glares, made impatient from sitting through the 
long sermon without breaks. "The word is speak by my earlier declaration."

"Speak then. The building of which you speak currently houses the Royal 
Conservatory! You are going to displace almost three hundred musicians."

The King shrugs, unconcerned. "We have no need for musicians. In fact, abolish 
them and then cut their budget! If they complain, arrest them and toss them in 
the Pit." His mind made up, King Goosen steps off the dais in search of relief 
for his aching bladder.

Bare furniture circles a cold stone hearth in this tiny cottage. The air is 
thick and all the curtains are closed in this gloomy tomb of a room. Over the 
fireplace, is a framed piece of sheet music with the title "Springtime Love".

leave." He motions you farther in. "Make yourself comfortable."

distance. "If you'll excuse me..." He stands and exits to the east.

events.intent: Play the Springtime Love melody with widow and butler present
events.response:
As you finish the melody, the widow and the butler can't help but to look at 
each other. Their eyes meet and the proverbial bell of love strikes midnight.

"Lovemuffin!"

"Sugarcakes!"

The two rise from their spots and embrace.

"I've loved you for a long time...ever since I cleaned your first teapot!"

"And I you...though I'd forgotten about it until this nice musician brought 
back old memories..."

"Oh darling, will you marry me?"

"Of course, sweetums. Could you ever doubt it?"

"My heart is so happy! You are the apple of my eye...the cream of my corn!"

The soap opera continues as butler Amoshtuff opens the eastern door and carries 
the new Mrs. Amoshtuff over the threshold. As the door closes, you smile, happy 
to have done your good deed for the day.

[You have earned two points for Cupid Substitution.] 

As you pull the trumpet away from your face, you suddenly realize that your 
tone quality has improved and your embouchure feels stronger than it has in 
ages. 

[Score 14, up 2]
>

Meanwhile, in King Goosen's Court...


"Sir hamster of Papoosen. You stand charged with crimes against the Crown and 
the good people of Papoosen! What do you have to say for yourself?" The Royal 
Judicator peers down over his spectacles at the rodent, who remains stoically 
and maddeningly silent.

"Psst!" The King beckons the Judicator behind his hand. "I thought we were 
eradicating hamsters. That is plainly a mouse."

The Judicator bends down to the throne and lowers his voice. "We are, Your 
Highness. But it would seem that hamsters have been nearly extinct for several 
years now. We could not find any deviants to arrest, and the man you declared 
to be hamster Persecutor ran away an hour ago after confiscating the funds of 
the Royal Conservatory. The best we could get on such short notice was this 
mouse."

The mouse runs along the dais, sniffing for food.

"Well why isn't it saying anything?" The King looks confused.

"Mice cannot talk, Your Highness."

Realizing the need to take charge of the situation for the benefit of the 
packed audience, the King pounds his fist against the armrest on his throne. 
"Now see here, you vile beast! You have had plenty of time to reflect upon your 
crimes and I simply shall not tolerate your silence an instant longer! Say what 
you have to say!"

The mouse looks up. "Squeak!"

Growling, the King snaps his fingers. "Guards! Throw violins at that hamster 
until it confesses!"

The Judicator looks up, surprised. "Violins??"

The King qualifies, "Nearly eighty of them, rotting away in the back room of 
the conservatory in sealed glass cases. Since the musicians no longer have 
their charter, I have decided to put them to better use. Guards, begin the 
violining of the criminal!"

Priceless maple wood shatters against the marble floor as the mouse makes its 
escape, unscathed.

Meanwhile, in King Goosen's Court...


Amidst the shattered remains of seventy-six violins, King Goosen and the Royal 
Advisor sit alone in the throne room. "Your Majesty, there is growing unrest in 
the kingdom. Currently, every citizen and everyone they have ever met are on 
double probation. Bards have disappeared from daily life, fearing arrest and 
fines. Inns are closing down for fear of brawls, since no one can release their 
emotions through song and dance with bards or instruments. The musicians of the 
Royal Conservatory are calling for your head and even some of the guards are 
joining in their protests!"

King Goosen broods over the events of the day, unsure of what direction to lead 
his people. "Revolts we have weathered, but never any so bad as this!"

The Advisor nods. "Especially since the protesters in this case are human and 
can speak in their own defense."

"Well, we shall just have to give them what they want. They want my head? Then 
they shall have it!"

"Shall I prepare the guillotine, Your Highness?"

"No no, nothing of the sort!" The King chuckles in a sudden burst of 
inspiration. "I shall have a commemorative coin pressed with my image! We can 
distribute them to the people of Papoosen and everyone will love me again."

The Royal Advisor quickly produces a castle inventory from his satchel. "It 
would seem that we're out of scrap metal. We may have to whittle them from 
pine."

"You'll do nothing of the sort! Why we just received a giant shipment of scrap 
brass an hour ago." He waves to the sealed crates in the corner.

"The TRUMPETS?!" The Advisor gasps as he reads the side of a crate. "But those 
are from the Conservatory! They are priceless beyond comparison..."

"Well," interjects the King, "they will be worth even more when they're melted 
down and stamped with my image! We shall call then 'Goosens'...in fact, by my 
royal decree, Goosens will be the new coin of the realm! Advisor, prepare a law 
to abolish gold and silver immediately." The Royal Advisor looks up at the sky 
and then sets to work outlining the latest royal proposal. "You will see, 
Advisor. I will win the love of my people yet! I am going to call for my supper 
now, and we shall begin melting down the trumpets at sundown!"

the room, including the snipers, who look horrified at being discovered. At a 
loss, since none of their training ever taught them what to do in a situation

events.response:
Aiming straight for the king, you play your medley in a plodding, but comical 
manner. The notes echo across the dais as a single duck falls through the 
skylight. Unlike the white ducks you're accustomed to, this one must weigh 
nearly fifty pounds! The retainers gasp and give warning, but the furious King 
is bent on your destruction. All eyes except for his watch the course of the 
fat duck, continuing on its inevitable course.

"Aieghh!" The duck lands on the King's head with mind-shattering ramifications. 
The duck survives, frazzled, but otherwise uninjured. The same can't be said 
for the King, who is sprawled on the carpet, out cold. The crowd edges closer 
to the fallen King, and one woman nudges him with her slipper. When it becomes 
apparent that the King won't wake up for quite some time, the court erupts in 
cheering and applause. The Royal Advisor is furiously patting you on the back 
when someone whoops with joy from the Upper Balcony.

[Hit any key.]
events.expected_outcome: The gravity-plus-duck effect defeats King Goosen and triggers the ending

events.intent: Press Return at the [Hit any key] pause to continue the ending cutscene
events.response:
Leonine swings down the wall hanging like a boy from a treehouse and runs up to 
the fallen King. "Clamouring cheetahs, he's down for the count!" The magician 
shakes your hand and winks. "Shows you what a little practice can do, eh?" When 
he sees your clueless look, he points at your trumpet.

The horn looks like it always has, its clean lines and shining silver a 
foreshadower of the music within. However, the bell is no longer glowing with 
magic. Shocked, you look to Leonine for explanation. He slaps his thigh and 
qualifies.

"Heck, I turned off that magic ages ago, silly neighbour! Everything you just 
did was the result of hard work and practice! Leapin' lemurs, who says that 
music isn't a little magical?" The crowd cheers madly and an older gentleman 
steps through the press.

"Great giraffes, it's Finney!" Leonine dives through the crowd and gives his 
old friend a big bear hug. A little embarassed by the sudden attention, the man 
pats Leonine on the back and turns his attentions to you.

"As this old coot has said, I am Finney...formerly Finney of Nolava, but now 
Finney the Augmented! I am third in a succession of musicians chosen to lead 
the Royal Conservatory of Papoosen." He points at the comatose King. "The 
talent I just saw today proves beyond a doubt that you're a fit candidate to be 
the fourth Augmented soul! I would be honoured if you would take my place and 
lead our musicians to a bright future. After all, King Goosen never did get the 
chance to melt down our trumpets!" He points to the corner where the crates sit.

Still shocked by your sudden turn of good luck, you can only stand in place, 
hoping a sudden gust of wind doesn't knock you over. Leonine elbows you in the 
ribs. "Say yes, neighbour! Finney and I need to catch up on old times, and he 
can't get away if he's got a position and a title and all that hodge-podge. But 
first, I think you'd better do something about Old Pudgy over there on the 
carpet." Looking at the inert body on the floor, a mischievous thought crosses 
your mind. You look up at Leonine and see that he's thinking the same thing. 
"Go for it, neighbour!"

One more time, you raise the trumpet to your lips and play. This special song, 
you dedicate to King Goosen and his many 'dedicated' years of service to 
Papoosen. Nothing happens at first, and you start to wonder if Leonine was 
pulling your leg.

Then a duck flies through the skylight...

...followed by a second, and a third.

Like a cacophonous mobile dinner party, a massive rain of ducks pours through 
the skylight. You count forty or fifty before you lose yourself in the sheer 
magnitude of the flock. The ducks settle around King Goosen and move him with 
their bills. Forming a living canvas underneath the King, the flock takes 
flight. Like a bug in a rug, the King is helplessly carried through the 
skylight by the ducks before disappearing over the horizon forever.

Perhaps "Ode to a Duck" was a good repertoire choice after all.
